title: Simultaneous normal-crossings subboundary charts and closed branch levels
statement: Let $X$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $B\subset X$ be a normal crossings divisor [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor], and let $D\subset B$ be a reduced closed subscheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] whose support is a union of irreducible components of $B$ [def-trf-union-of-irreducible-components]. The empty union is allowed. Use the neighborhood convention for normal crossings of Stacks Tag 0BSF: every geometric point has a pointed etale neighborhood $V\to X$ with $V$ regular and Noetherian, on which, at every $v\in V$, the ideal of $B_V$ is a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{V,v}$. This neighborhood condition is part of the hypothesis; it is stronger than merely asking for a presentation at the chosen stalk in [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor]. For every geometric point $\bar x$ there is a pointed affine etale neighborhood $e:W=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], with chosen point $w$ over $\bar x$, and regular functions $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ such that their germs form a regular system of parameters at $w$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and, for some $0\le s\le r\le d$, the scheme-theoretic equations on $W$ are $D_W=V(t_1\cdots t_s)$ and $B_W=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$. The scheme $W$ is regular and Noetherian. At every $u\in W$, the germs of those $t_j$, $1\le j\le r$, which vanish at $u$ are distinct members of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{W,u}$. All the displayed factors vanish at $w$; factors invertible at the chosen point have been removed by shrinking. The number $b_D(\bar x)$ of geometric branches [def-trf-normal-crossings-branch-count] is independent of these presentations, is invariant under etale pullback, and on $W$ equals $\#\{1\le j\le s:t_j(u)=0\text{ in }\kappa(u)\}$. For each integer $k\ge1$, the inverse image of $T_k=\{x:b_D(x)\ge k\}$ is the finite union $\bigcup_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\},\ |J|=k}V(t_j:j\in J)$, and $T_k$ is closed in $X$. If $X$ is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), then $b_D$ is bounded by a finite integer.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2 and 4.1.6--4.1.8, printed pp. 117--118: simultaneous boundary coordinates and the multiplicity stratification; geometric-branch interpretation as in the item.

proof.text: Fix $\bar x$. Choose the pointed neighborhood $V$ in the explicit neighborhood hypothesis. At its chosen point $w$, take a full parameter system with $B_V$ generated by its first $r$ factors. Restrict to an affine open around $w$ and represent all parameter germs by functions there. This affine is Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The equality of the ideal of $B_V$ with the principal product holds after shrinking: both ideals are finitely generated in the affine Noetherian ring, and each of the finitely many containments holding after localization holds after inverting one element outside the prime of $w$. Intersect these finitely many principal opens. Call the resulting affine $W$ and its functions $t_1,\ldots,t_d$. The lift of $\bar x$ is retained by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink]. Thus $B_W=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ scheme-theoretically and all displayed factors vanish at $w$.

source.place: Tag 0BSF, definition-normal-crossings; Tag 0BI9, definition-strict-normal-crossings; finite-generator localization of the stalk equation

proof.text: The pointwise parameter hypothesis holds everywhere on $W$, so [lem-sfb-snc-boundary-parameter-criterion] gives its strict normal crossings boundary structure. In particular its finitely many reduced irreducible components $C_a$ are regular. Apply [lem-trf-etale-component-coordinate-identification] with $X=W$, $D=B_W$, and the identity etale map, using the equation from Step 1. After shrinking around $w$, its components are precisely the hyperplanes $C_i=V(t_i)$ for $1\le i\le r$; components missing $w$ have been removed. At any other $u$ apply the same identification to the identity map and a parameter presentation of $B_W$ at $u$. It assigns the components through $u$ to distinct parameter hyperplanes. Thus each $t_i$ vanishing at $u$ generates the same principal ideal as its assigned parameter. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] the local ring is a domain. In this domain the two generators differ by a unit; multiplying the corresponding parameter by that unit retains a full parameter system. This proves the required uniform distinct-parameter condition for the fixed functions $t_i$.

source.place: Tags 0BIA, lemma-strict-normal-crossings, and 0BI9: components correspond to parameter prime ideals

proof.text: Let $C$ be an irreducible component of $D_W$. Its generic point maps to a component-generic point of $D$: the map $D_W\to D$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. On affine charts its ring map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], the source generic prime is minimal. Going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] shows that its contraction is minimal too: a strictly smaller contracted prime would lift to a strictly smaller source prime. Hence the generic image is generic in a component of $D$, which by hypothesis is a component of $B$. Since $C$ is contained in $B_W$, it is contained in some $C_i$. The generic point of $C_i$ maps to the generic point of a component of $B$, by the same flat going-down argument. Its image generalizes that of the generic point of $C$; both are component-generic in $B$, so the images agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], the fibre of $B_W\to B$ has discrete topology. Two comparable points of that fibre are therefore equal. Consequently $C=C_i$. Thus $|D_W|$ is the union of a subset of the hyperplanes $C_i$.

source.place: Tags 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; 03HV, lemma-generalizations-lift-flat; 02GL, lemma-etale-fibres; component selection argument

proof.text: Renumber the selected hyperplanes as $1,\ldots,s$. The pullback $D_W$ is reduced by [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]. At $u\in W$ discard those selected $t_i$ which are units. The remaining factors are distinct regular parameters by Step 2. They are prime in the regular local domain by [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization]. Their product generates a radical ideal: if the product divides $a^n$, each prime factor divides $a$, and their pairwise nonassociate prime factors therefore have product dividing $a$. The empty product generates the unit ideal. Hence $V(t_1\cdots t_s)$ is reduced and has exactly the support found in Step 3. Uniqueness of reduced induced closed structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] gives $D_W=V(t_1\cdots t_s)$ as closed subschemes. This proves both simultaneous equations, including $D_W=\varnothing$ when $s=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD; schemes.tex Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme; ILO VIII 4.1.8

proof.text: For $s\ge1$, [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-max-stratum] identifies the count $\#\{j\le s:t_j(u)=0\}$ with the number of minimal primes of the reduced strict henselian local ring of $D_W$, and proves its coordinate independence and etale invariance. To compare with every germ presentation allowed in [def-trf-normal-crossings-branch-count], apply [lem-trf-parameter-product-strict-local-branches] to its regular local chart ring and its selected parameters: its length equals the number of strict-local minimal primes. For the etale map from that chart to $X$, [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies the ambient strict localizations at the same geometric point. Pulling back the defining ideal therefore identifies the strict-local divisor quotients. Thus all presentation lengths equal our coordinate count; their set is a singleton and its infimum is that count. For $s=0$ the same strict-local quotient is the zero ring and the branch lemma gives length zero for every presentation. Formula, coordinate independence and etale invariance follow in all cases; for an arbitrary etale pullback use the pulled-back atlas [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change].

source.place: VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, printed p.118: multiplicity interpreted as geometric branches

proof.text: Fix $k\ge1$. At $u$, the inequality $b_D(e(u))\ge k$ says exactly that some $k$-element subset of $\{1,\ldots,s\}$ vanishes there. Thus $e^{-1}(T_k)=\bigcup_{|J|=k}V(t_j:j\in J)$, a finite union of closed subsets, empty for $k>s$. In particular $W\setminus e^{-1}(T_k)$ is open. Its image is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. By Step 5 that image lies in $X\setminus T_k$. Conversely every point outside $T_k$ lifts to one of our charts and lies in that image. Hence $X\setminus T_k$ is the union of these open images, proving that $T_k$ is closed.

source.place: VIII 4.1.6--4.1.8, p.118; morphisms.tex Tag 03WT, lemma-etale-open: closedness by open images of chart complements

proof.text: The images $e(W)$ form an open covering of $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. If $X$ is quasi-compact, choose finitely many charts covering it. On the image of each chart Step 5 bounds the branch count by its finite selected-list length $s$. Their maximum bounds $b_D$ on $X$. If $X$ is empty, use the bound zero. This also covers $B=\varnothing$, $D=\varnothing$, zero-dimensional stalks and charts with no selected factors.

source.place: VIII 4.1.6, p.118: finite depth; finite subcover argument

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q44-6ba89c0d1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full: all 7 steps and every cited statement. Sources checked at the cited places: Stacks etale.tex 0BI9 (l.2396), 0BSF (l.2522) and 0CBS (l.2679, including its proof), and ILO VIII 4.1.2–4.1.8 (printed pp.117–118). There are no new nodes. The live item is still unsplit, there is no repair note, and the only citer is lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup (landed by Q111). The only statement change is two added sentences that make the Stacks 0BSF neighbourhood hypothesis explicit: a pointed étale neighbourhood on which the parameter condition holds at every point. This change is justified. def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor is the pointwise condition (2) of 0CBS, which matches 0BSF only for J-2 or Nagata schemes, so the base statement's chart-wide parameter condition and the closedness of T_k could not be derived from it. ILO 4.1.2 uses the étale-local meaning, and the caller's own prose ('etale locally has equation t_1⋯t_r=0') supplies the new hypothesis. Step checks: (1) the stalk ideal equality spreads to an affine neighbourhood; the affine-shrink lemma keeps the lift. (2) The SNC criterion gives regular components; component-coordinate identification at w and at each other u gives t_i equal to a unit times σ_j in a domain, so the fixed t_i are uniform parameters. (3) Flat going down (direction checked), the minimal-prime lemma, sobriety and the discrete étale fibre show that each component of D_W is a whole C_i; the self-intersecting component case was checked. (4) Reduced pullback, distinct prime parameters with a squarefree product, and uniqueness of the reduced induced structure give D_W=V(t_1⋯t_s). (5) The max-stratum lemma, the parameter-product strict-local branch count and ind-étale strict-local invariance show that every presentation length in the definition is the same, so the infimum is the coordinate count; s=0 is handled. (6) T_k is closed because étale images of chart complements are open. (7) Quasi-compactness gives a finite bound. Edge cases checked: B=∅, D=∅, D=B, k>s, dimension 0, xy=0. The nine declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. No SGA source is used. Maintainer notes: either change def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor to the 0BSF meaning or keep the explicit hypothesis; the caller's step 1 should state that it reads its hypothesis in the 0BSF sense.
